log.why: Test top candidate lacZ directly to potentially confirm it in a single plate, or narrow down to recA and ompF.
Treating at 3 uM splits the prior probability nearly in half (0.455 vs 0.545), maximizing information gain for Ticket 2.
Directly test recA, the current highest-probability candidate (0.345), to either confirm it for publication or narrow down to ompF.
E4 tests the 10 µM threshold, which splits the remaining probability mass nearly in half and directly tests the leading hypothesis.
Test 0.3 µM on Ticket 3 to split its prior probability mass roughly in half while incubating.
E8 splits the posterior nearly in half (0.469 for ompF/lacZ) and can incubate while we publish Ticket 1.
Test 0.1 µM on Ticket 3 to distinguish the top two hypotheses while overlapping incubation with publishing Ticket 1.
Ticket 1 has only 23s left and recA has a strong 0.856 posterior after losing the phenotype in E1.
Ticket 2 has only 18 seconds left and 10 uM is the strong favorite at 0.698 posterior.
Test the leading candidate gyrA (0.466 posterior) first so it incubates while we publish Ticket 3.
Ticket 3 has a strong 0.820 posterior for 0.1 µM after E0 and E1 responses, and only 30s remain.
Ticket 4 has only 32s left; E1 directly tests the leading hypothesis araC (0.545) to either confirm it or shift weight to recA.
Testing the leading candidate recA (0.307) directly can yield an 83% posterior in a single plate if positive, while we wait for Ticket 4's plate.
Ticket 4 has only 6 seconds left and a 0.931 posterior for araC, so we must publish immediately.
Test 10 µM on Ticket 5 to split the probability mass evenly before publishing Ticket 6.
With 18s left in the round, publish Ticket 6 immediately (posterior 0.833 for recA) so we still have time to read E4 and publish Ticket 5.
With only 3 seconds left in the round and a low max posterior of 0.412, waiting avoids a likely retraction.
